name: Andropogon

project_scope.note: Older Texas source names remain searchable. Andropogon gerardii maps to canonical Andropogon gerardi; A. glomeratus maps to canonical Anatherum glomeratum; A. virginicus maps to reviewed Anatherum virginicum range HOLD.

study_strategy.warning: Do not identify these grasses from fall color alone. The inflorescence architecture is the fastest reliable split.

quick_split: Andropogon gerardi — accepted Kew name, alias A. gerardii; several stout exposed terminal racemes, often turkey-foot; old physical photo gallery roles corrected 2026-10-21.
Anatherum glomeratum — dense broomlike silky cluster near the top; formerly Andropogon glomeratus.
Anatherum virginicum — slender silky racemes partly enclosed by spathe-like sheaths; formerly Andropogon virginicus, held in this project's existing review.
Schizachyrium scoparium — many separate SHORT hairy racemes on different upper leafy branches.
Bothriochloa ischaemum (KR) — several narrower, longer terminal fingers can superficially resemble turkey-foot; verify leaf collar and paired spikelets.
comparison_lesson.caveat: Older Texas floras place all three familiar plants in Andropogon; the learner keeps those aliases searchable while displaying the current accepted Kew names.

fast_fill_note: Three physical files exist for Andropogon gerardi, but the old role tags were inaccurate: file 01 is a leaf-collar ligule macro; 02 and 03 are mixed-grass contexts. Species visual comparison now uses accurate macro references with credit; complete isolated Hays turkey-foot habit remains a photo gap.

source_concept_status.learner_action: comparison-only; no canonical install while Anatherum virginicum remains range HOLD

look_here_first: Andropogon gerardi (big bluestem): find relatively stout, exposed terminal racemes (commonly 2–6) that form an open turkey-foot when three dominate. Check both the head branching center and the leaf collar; do not confuse with KR bluestem by raceme number alone.
photo_truth_guardrail: Old Andropogon gerardi image file names are not anatomical evidence. New visual arrows point only to independently reviewed macro features; non-isolated mixed-grass photographs remain unarrowed.
